subject: GitHub Models retirement and Microsoft Foundry migration boundary

selection.reason: GitHub completed the retirement of a developer-facing inference service on 2026-07-30. On the Seoul publication morning, credential-free probes made the previously announced change directly observable as HTTP 410 on both catalog and inference routes, while current official quickstart and REST pages still advertised the retired success path. Official Foundry documents expose a concrete deployment, identity, billing, and endpoint migration boundary useful to software engineers.

signals.note: Reviewed recent OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI, GitHub Copilot, Moonshot AI, and model-release surfaces. Search snippets and announcement summaries were used only to find primary pages.

Reviewed GitHub Changelog, NVIDIA developer, AMD developer and ROCm, Hugging Face, vLLM, SGLang, and recent hardware-software release surfaces. No search result or secondary report is cited as article evidence.

Opened current X profile surfaces for Noam Brown, Shunyu Yao, Percy Liang, and Sayash Kapoor and ran recent-post searches. Direct profile pages exposed no usable post content in the available public response and search results did not identify a material new primary artifact, so X contributed no article fact or source.

claims.claim: GitHub announced GitHub Models fully retired on 2026-07-30, and credential-free probes at 2026-07-31T08:05:31+09:00 and 08:05:32+09:00 observed HTTP 410 on the public catalog and chat completions routes.
claims.method: Opened GitHub's July 30 retirement announcement, then issued a credential-free GET to /catalog/models and a credential-free POST with a minimal synthetic JSON body to /inference/chat/completions. Both returned HTTP 410 and the same 152-byte JSON body with SHA-256 eb684b77670c904f8a8ac2304cacadd359f792928a5ff14d502912342ee84afd.

sources.limitations: Vendor-authored product status establishes GitHub's retirement decision but is not an independent measurement of every account path.
Credential-free GET does not establish account-specific authenticated behavior and the response body may change after observation.

sources.limitations: No GitHub token or paid model call was used, so response schema after authentication was not tested.

claims.method: Opened the Microsoft upgrade and endpoint documents, compared prerequisites, model deployment semantics, endpoint forms, key and Entra ID authentication, and the stated August 26, 2026 Azure AI Inference beta SDK retirement. No Azure resource was created.

claims.claim: The observed retirement body uses temporary-brownout wording, but RFC 9110 defines HTTP 410 for unavailable resources whose condition is likely permanent; combined with GitHub's retirement announcement, clients should not classify this response as an unbounded transient retry.
claims.method: Compared RFC 9110 section 15.5.11, GitHub's full-retirement statement, and the exact 410 response body observed on both endpoints.

sources.owner: IETF HTTP Working Group / RFC Editor
sources.limitations: The standard defines status semantics but does not determine GitHub's internal rollout duration.
The error code or message may change after observation.
Product announcement does not prescribe client retry implementation.

limitations: The article recommends a bounded operational classification and does not claim GitHub will never alter the endpoint response.
Existing queued jobs may need provider-specific replay and idempotency handling not covered by HTTP status alone.
conflict_of_interest: GitHub controls its endpoint response and retirement messaging.
recheck_triggers: GitHub publishes explicit retry or migration error semantics
The body no longer uses the brownout code
